subject: Renewal pricing: invoice smoothing, capacity uplift & rate safeguard
messages:
From: Natalie Cohen <natalie.cohen@brightsidehealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightsidehealth.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — smoothing invoices + capacity uplift

Hi Jonas / Laura,

Hope you're both well. We're starting internal planning for our July renewal and want to surface a couple constraints and asks so we can avoid last-minute pushback from procurement. High-level:

- Usage is trending +40% YoY; we'll need ~30% more peak capacity for Q3/Q4.
- Our finance team prefers smoothing larger annual invoices into even monthly/quarterly payments for forecasting.
- Procurement asked whether Redwood will entertain a temporary price-hold (first 6 months of the new term) while we validate performance after capacity increase.

Attached is our March usage extract so you can see the run-rate. Can you share a short note with options (discount ladder for commit, credits for unused burst, and a proposed payment cadence) we can take to procurement next week? Also please highlight any conditions (minimum commit, true-up cadence, SLA adjustments) that matter.

Thanks — Natalie
Natalie Cohen
Head of Cloud Partnerships
Brightside Health
Attachments: brightside_usage_Mar2027.pdf (pdf)
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Natalie Cohen <natalie.cohen@brightsidehealth.com>, Peter Liao <peter.liao@brightsidehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — smoothing invoices + capacity uplift

Natalie — thanks for the usage extract. Quick read; happy to propose a structure so you can brief procurement. High-level options below (we can make any of these a formal amendment).

Option A — Staged commit + invoice smoothing (recommended for scale-ups)- 12-month term with an initial 6-month price-hold at current blended effective rate; months 7–12 move to negotiated rate.- Commit: baseline = current 12-mo run-rate; month 1–3 uplift allowance (burst) of +30% included; any sustained usage above baseline+30% triggers a true-up at month 3.- Discounts: 8% blended discount for a 12-month commit; additional 3% if you prepay 3 months upfront.- Billing cadence: we can issue equal monthly invoices (invoice smoothing) with one true-up at month 3 and final reconciliation at month 12.- Credits: unused committed burst capacity will convert to a one-time credit applied at month 6.

Option B — Conservative commit + burst buffer- 12-month term; no initial price-hold but tiered discounts based on realized consumption bands.- Lower minimum commit, higher overage rate, immediate true-ups quarterly.

Operational notes:
- SLA/latency targets remain unchanged; if capacity uplift requires dedicated pools we can convert to a reserved-capacity addendum (pricing separate).
- We recommend Option A for Brightside given the scale and desire to protect rate during validation.

I'm attaching a draft amendment (RI_draft-amendment_renewal-v2.pdf) and an itemized line breakdown (line-item-breakdown_Q3-Q4.xlsx) to make it easier for procurement. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call with procurement this week.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: RI_draft-amendment_renewal-v2.pdf (pdf); line-item-breakdown_Q3-Q4.xlsx (xlsx)
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Natalie Cohen <natalie.cohen@brightsidehealth.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — smoothing invoices + capacity uplift

Quick note — I've run the numbers on Option A: the one-time credit for unused burst is capped at 20% of the uplift allowance to prevent open-ended liabilities. Also adding a clause: procurement must request conversion to Dedicated (reserved capacity) at least 45 days prior to expected dedicated cutover; lead times vary by region.

I'll prepare a short 1-pager summary (cost delta + procurement checklist) for Natalie to share. Priyom — can you validate the SLA language for the price-hold period?

Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Account Strategy
Redwood Inference
From: Peter Liao <peter.liao@brightsidehealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Natalie Cohen <natalie.cohen@brightsidehealth.com>, procurement@brightsidehealth.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — smoothing invoices + capacity uplift

Thanks Jonas / Laura — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from procurement: 

1) They want the invoice smoothing to be predictable monthly equal invoices (not quarterly) if possible — that helps our ledger.
2) The price-hold is acceptable if there is a clear performance validation plan (we'll want latency percentiles and error-rate targets for months 1–6).
3) Please provide a single-sheet cost comparison (current vs Option A blended vs Option B) and a DocuSign-ready amendment so procurement can sign once stakeholders approve.

We'll aim to get an internal decision by May 3. Adding procurement on this thread.

— Peter
Peter Liao
Lead, Cloud Procurement
Brightside Health
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Natalie Cohen <natalie.cohen@brightsidehealth.com>, Peter Liao <peter.liao@brightsidehealth.com>, procurement@brightsidehealth.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 May 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — smoothing invoices + capacity uplift

Peter / Natalie — thanks, understood. Attached is the one-page cost comparison and updated amendment with:

- Monthly equal invoices (12 equal installments) with a mid-term true-up at month 3 and final reconciliation at month 12.
- 6-month price-hold at current effective rate (performance validation appendix added: 95th percentile p99 latency target, error-rate ceiling, and monthly reporting cadence).
- Unused uplift credit capped at 20% of uplift dollars, applied as a credit on month 6 invoice.
- Conversion to Dedicated requires signed notice 45 days before requested date and may carry a separate onboarding fee.

DocuSign link: https://app.redwood.example/docusign/BD-2024-179
Drive: https://drive.redwood.example/drive/folders/BRIGHTSIDE-RENEWAL-2027
Attachments: line-item-breakdown_Q3-Q4.xlsx; RI_draft-amendment_renewal-v2.pdf

If procurement confirms by May 3, we can have the signed amendment and a July 1 effective date. Happy to schedule a 20-minute walkthrough for the finance/procurement team tomorrow.

Best — Jonas
